Set the camera positions for the solve.

Use 'Nodal' to place cameras at a single nodal point. Use 'Spherical' to position cameras on a sphere. Use 'Horizontal' to position cameras on a horizontal line. Use 'Vertical' to position cameras on a vertical line. Use 'Planar' to position cameras on a plane. Use 'Free' to not enforce any constraint on the camera positions.

Convergence changes are only supported where there is parallax between cameras, 'converge' will have no effect with a 'Nodal' solve as there is no separation between the camera positions.

Note: Horizontal, Vertical, Planar, and Free layout are experimental. In some cases the generated solves will be less accurate than the Spherical and Nodal ones.

Select the lens distortion calculation for the camera solve.

Use 'No Lens Distortion' if the source footage has already been corrected to remove distortion. Use 'Known' to fix the existing lens distortion in the solve. Optimize 'per Camera' to refine the lens distortion for each camera. Optimize 'Single' to calculate a single lens model for all cameras.

description.plain_text: C_CameraSolver 2.1v5: Connect and analyse input footage from a rig to define the camera metadata ready for stitching. Input: Connect inputs to automatically setup views for stitching. Choose a preset rig definition or alternatively set the global camera parameters. This defines the default rig configuration used in matching and solving. Keying: Set analysis keys where there is structure in the overlap region between images. The input footage is matched at the analysis keys to calculate the relative pose between each camera. Analysis: Set the analysis options for the solve. Choose the type of focal length and distortion expected for the rig, and the camera layout. Analyse the sequence by matching and solving. A rig preset can be refined directly without an initial solve. Toolbox: The viewer toolbox can be used to review and delete the feature matches, create user defined matches, review the error for connected cameras and correct the horizon. Output: The image alignment is shown as a preview in the main view. Set the output format for the preview, you can also project the inputs to the panorama for manual stitching. Cameras: The cameras table shows the calculated metadata for the rig, this is passed downstream for image stitching and image projections. Camera parameters can be adjusted individually or as group under the 'Cameras' tab. Export: Export the camera setup.
description.text:
C_CameraSolver 2.1v5: Connect and analyse input footage from a rig to define the camera metadata ready for stitching.

Input: Connect inputs to automatically setup views for stitching. Choose a preset rig definition or alternatively set the global camera parameters. This defines the default rig configuration used in matching and solving.

Keying: Set analysis keys where there is structure in the overlap region between images. The input footage is matched at the analysis keys to calculate the relative pose between each camera.

Analysis: Set the analysis options for the solve. Choose the type of focal length and distortion expected for the rig, and the camera layout. Analyse the sequence by matching and solving. A rig preset can be refined directly without an initial solve.

Toolbox: The viewer toolbox can be used to review and delete the feature matches, create user defined matches, review the error for connected cameras and correct the horizon.

Output: The image alignment is shown as a preview in the main view. Set the output format for the preview, you can also project the inputs to the panorama for manual stitching.

Cameras: The cameras table shows the calculated metadata for the rig, this is passed downstream for image stitching and image projections. Camera parameters can be adjusted individually or as group under the 'Cameras' tab.

Export: Export the camera setup.
